items.rationale: Sections 2.4.4 and 7.1.9 cover like-for-like replacement of the internal frost-fractured valve. One valve is estimated at €52 gross using the reference price.
Sections 2.4.4 and 7.1.9 cover connection elements that need renewal with the fractured fitting. One standard hose is estimated at €27 gross.
Sections 7.1.7(f) and 7.1.9 cover necessary repair labour. Three hours at the reference rate of about €98 gross give approximately €295; the separate return-trip charge is assessed on its own.

Sections 7.1.7(e) and 7.1.9 cover consumables actually used in the repair, but §3.6(c) excludes the contractor's own small equipment. The generic line does not establish what was used; €8 gross allows for minor documented consumables if accepted.
Sections 7.1.9 and 7.1.11 allow one attendance for covered repair work. The closest same-wording reference supports €41 gross for the initial vehicle charge.
Sections 2.4.6, 3.6(c) and 5.2.2 expressly cover imaging equipment used to locate the insured escape. An equipment-use charge of €45 gross is within the €2,500 per-event leak-location cap.
Section 7.1.11 excludes a separately billed return attendance unless agreed in advance, and no approval is stated. If approval were documented, €41 gross is the allowance for one comparable trip.

items.description: Remove loose and spalled facade plaster
items.rationale: The facade frost endorsement activates §2.6.2, which covers removal of failed material from the damaged area. Two localized removals at about €45 each total €90 gross, excluding separately billed access and disposal.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(d) cover like-for-like base plaster on the frost-damaged patches. Allow €65 gross for the material, with substrate work and painter labour billed separately.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(c) cover re-forming the damaged substrate. Allow €130 gross for localized preparation and levelling, without paying again for base plaster or separately billed hours.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7 cover priming required by the existing finish system. Allow €45 gross for the affected area, without duplicating separately billed labour.

Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(c) cover necessary drying before reinstatement, but not ordinary waiting for plaster to cure. If an active drying measure was needed and performed, allow €65 gross for a modest localized treatment.

Sections 2.6.2, 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(d) cover only the coats required by the pre-loss finish system on the damaged area, not automatically all four billed coats. Allow €125 gross for the necessary finish, with labour billed separately.

Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(f) cover labour attributable to the damaged elevation, not the undamaged rear. Five covered hours at €65 gross give €325; any rear-elevation hours must be removed from the allowance.

Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.8 cover necessary access, with no split for rear work because the scaffold was struck before that work began. About 48 m² of two-storey scaffold at roughly €14/m² gross gives an allowance of €675.
Sections 2.6.3(a), 7.1.5 and 7.1.6 exclude repainting a separate undamaged elevation, even for colour matching. €600 gross is a conditional market estimate only, not an allowance under this policy.
Sections 2.6.2 and 5.2.1 cover transport and disposal of material removed from the frost-damaged area. A few rubble sacks support a €55 gross disposal allowance rather than a skip charge.
Sections 3.6(b) and 7.1.12 exclude administrative charges that price no repair work. €10 gross is a conditional estimate only.
Sections 3.6(a) and 7.1.12 exclude contractor subsistence even when the underlying work is covered. Three refreshments at €7 each give a conditional estimate of €21 gross only.
